elections.quote: Yeah, me too. I only made a comment about *where* I think they *should* vote, which apparently was fascism :)
Show me where I argued for disenfranchising anyone.

think, for example, of Arkansans in college voting in Madison or Ann Arbor or Boston

low-impact to those votes

There is NO DOUBT that GOPers want to make it harder to vote on campus. 
That's not my project. I just don't want college kids floating bond issues in small towns :)

I think "the place your parents are and the house with your stuff in it" edges out "a dorm you just arrived in."

See, I don't care about where you vote for a national election. My beef is with kids voting in *local* elections, esp on money issues.

I think there's not much you can do to overcome the short attention span of young people when it comes to voting. And while I agree that "just open polling places where they are" is necessary right now, I still think that drains off Dem votes that could have more effect in their hometowns.
